title: Pieces relabeled as a suite
summary: He resents others relabeling his pieces as a suite.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: There was also a discussion of the 'Tonsillectomy' and two others were supposed to be part of a suite.
Jack said that and you said at one point the same thing, but on the back of one of those scores, which I have, you had written part of 'Jitterbug Suite' or first
movement of "Jitterbug Suite" or something--or somebody had written it--Boyd may have written it after you delivered it to him. It's on one of those scores.
That's crazy, that's really crazy. It's not true.

Everybody was trying to make something significant, they were trying to make symphony out of jazz or make serious music out of jazz or whatever nomenclature applies, and Dorsey asked Stravinsky to write something for him, as I remember.

Stravinsky wrote something--or was it Goodman--one or the other, and Stravinsky did that thing with Woody and Bela Bartok, I think Goodman asked--I've forgotten but everyone was taking themself terribly seriously in those days and it seemed appropriate that they were trying to make a suite out of it, par-
ticularly your music. Maybe the recording people wanted to do that.

I don't know who was responsible; whoever it was, he was an idiot, or maybe a good businessman; I really don't know. I always become offended when people take my work and relabel it and restructure it and try to create something out of a few pieces of work that was never intended, never written that way or was not related.
